query: Consider the following context: High-temperature self-lubricating materials with stable tribological performance across a wide temperature range are essential for advanced mechanical systems under extreme conditions. However, balancing mechanical strength and lubrication efficiency remains a key challenge. In that context, which material can be used for high-performance wide-temperature self-lubricating materials, and why?

generation.hypothesis: The addition of graphene nanoparticles to a titanium alloy matrix will enhance its self-lubricating properties and maintain mechanical strength across a wide temperature range.
generation.material_initial_state: Titanium alloy (Ti-6Al-4V) in its initial development stage
generation.intervention: Adding 1-2 wt% graphene nanoparticles to the titanium alloy matrix through powder metallurgy
generation.conditions: Sintering at 1200°C for 2 hours under a high-purity argon atmosphere with a flow rate of 10 mL/min
generation.mechanism: The graphene nanoparticles will form a solid lubricant film on the surface through a combination of mechanical and chemical interactions, reducing friction and wear, while the titanium alloy matrix will provide mechanical strength and stability
generation.predicted_outcome: A 30% reduction in friction coefficient and a 25% increase in wear resistance compared to the baseline titanium alloy, across a temperature range of 20-500°C with a temperature stability of ±10°C
generation.boundary: Temperature range: 20-500°C, Load: 100-500 N, Sliding speed: 0.1-1 meter per second
generation.uncertainty: The actual performance of the graphene-reinforced titanium alloy may vary depending on the quality of the graphene nanoparticles, the sintering process, and the testing conditions.

falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the friction coefficient is not reduced by at least 25% or the wear rate is not decreased by at least 20% compared to the baseline, the hypothesis is falsified
